answer: Persistent pairwise interaction ledger. Each identity accumulates a lantern score only through sustained reciprocal exchange with distinct peers, and a new account starts dark, so manufactured identities must each spend months of genuine compute and human attention to glow. An ember of trust transfers only along already-verified edges, capping how fast a cluster can bootstrap itself, while the atlas of all edges is public and anomaly detection flags dense inner rings. An attacker pays the full interaction cost per identity with no shortcut, making each fake node as expensive as a real one.
